{{Short description|Boolean algebra with unary operators expressing necessity and possibility modalities}}
{{one source |date=May 2024}}
In [[abstract algebra|algebra]] and [[logic]], a '''modal algebra''' is a structure <math>\langle A,\land,\lor,-,0,1,\Box\rangle</math> such that
*<math>\langle A,\land,\lor,-,0,1\rangle</math> is a [[Boolean algebra (structure)|Boolean algebra]],
*<math>\Box</math> is a unary operation on ''A'' satisfying <math>\Box1=1</math> and <math>\Box(x\land y)=\Box x\land\Box y</math> for all ''x'', ''y'' in ''A''.
Modal algebras provide models of [[propositional logic|propositional]] [[modal logic]]s in the same way as Boolean algebras are models of [[classical logic]]. In particular, the [[variety (universal algebra)|variety]] of all modal algebras is the equivalent algebraic semantics of the modal logic ''K'' in the sense of [[abstract algebraic logic]], and the [[lattice (order)|lattice]] of its subvarieties is dually [[isomorphic]] to the lattice of [[normal modal logic]]s.

[[Stone's representation theorem]] can be generalized to the [[Jónsson–Tarski duality]], which ensures that each modal algebra can be [[representation theorem|represented]] as the algebra of admissible sets in a modal [[general frame]].

A '''Magari algebra''' (or '''diagonalizable algebra''') is a modal algebra satisfying <math>\Box (-\Box x \lor x) = \Box x</math>. Magari algebras correspond to [[provability logic]] and are named after {{Interlanguage link|Roberto Magari|it}}.
